clubs.name: Purdue Stack
clubs.description:
Stack is Purdue's premier software engineering organization. Each semester, we partner with companies to provide student members the opportunity to work on projects for those companies. Additionally, we host speaker events, workshops, and cross-club collaborations.

Real clients, real deadlines — we ship software that reaches real users. Members connect with like-minded builders, mentors, and industry professionals, and learn from engineers, founders, and leaders at the companies you want to work at.

clubs.name: Hack The Future
clubs.description:
Creating Software for Nonprofits
Hack the Future is a student organization at Purdue aimed towards creating software for local nonprofits. We develop several projects throughout the school year with various different nonprofits with the hopes of bettering the community.

We are actively involved with the community and provide software development services at no cost to nonprofits! Hack the Future is comprised of students all working together to develop amazing projects.

clubs.name: Build Purdue
clubs.description:
buildpurdue is Purdue University's student-run entrepreneurship community. Go from idea to launch with our cohort program, Nightshift co-working sessions, and founder events at Purdue.

Whether you're still sketching out a concept or already shipping to users, buildpurdue is where Purdue's founders find their people.

clubs.name: Humanoid Robot Club
clubs.description:
Small Step for a Robot. Giant Leap for Robotics.
The Humanoid Robot Club is building NEMO, a humanoid robot, with the vision of being the first group of students to build a humanoid robot that goes to space and does what an astronaut and a rover can and cannot do.

NEMO runs 18 actuators with 12 degrees of freedom across its legs, driven by a deep reinforcement learning control stack built with MuJoCo and JAX and deployed on ROS2. In December 2025 it took its first steps on the ground, moving the project out of simulation and into the real world.

With 1500+ members, the club also runs StarkHacks, the world's largest hardware hackathon.

clubs.name: Boiler Exams
clubs.description: Boilerexams was founded in 2020 by two Purdue freshmen who saw a need for a studying platform to help students adapt to the college exam environment. The first iteration was built in a few weeks over the summer and deployed for the first midterm cycle of fall 2020. It grew in popularity over the years, but its hastily designed site limited the founders’ ability to expand. In the spring of 2023, they began recruiting a team for a full redesign. Now, with a fresh new look, Boilerexams is better than ever. Enjoy new courses, better statistics, and the smoothest studying experience we could dream up.

clubs.name: Boiler Classes
clubs.description:
BoilerClasses
is an unofficial catalog for Purdue courses made by Purdue students,
based in West Lafayette, Indiana. BoilerClasses is a simple Next.js app with a few Python helper files to format and organize the data. We use a Redis instance to store and rapidly query all our data.

We use Fly.io through Docker to host our app. More steps to run the Docker container through our Dockerfile can be found below.

clubs.name: Boiler Bookings
clubs.description:
Letter from the devs: 
Hi. We’re college students who made BoilerBookings.com to make it easier to travel home for breaks. After people actually started using it, we brought on nine chillers to help.

Booking trips with shuttles is already hard enough. But then, we noticed that airlines try to squeeze every dollar out of us with erratic prices.

As broke college students (and a bunch of CS majors) we made Jumpseat to solve these problems. Hopefully, it helps you out. If not, please email us to let us know.

clubs.name: Autonomous Robot Club
clubs.description:
The Autonomous Robotics Club of Purdue was created to grow the skills and abilities of its members through design projects centered around advanced autonomous robotics systems. It provides hands-on, real world experience to interdisciplinary teams using industry standard tools and practices.

Through ARC, members can meet like-minded individuals, solve real world robotics problems, gain experience with industry-standard tools, and build their career portfolios. We welcome new members of any skill level and provide an environment for members to learn about topics such as state estimation, control algorithms, and machine learning. New members have opportunities for leadership early on and can gain in depth experience working on projects that interest them. ARC projects typically include a mix of hardware and software design.
